assumptions.summary: Neglect chemical erosion because the target is ordinary sandcastles lasting hours to roughly one day.
Treat the nearby coastline as straight because the foundation diameter is small relative to coastline curvature.
Treat rainfall as constant over the small foundation area and short modeled interval.
Exclude human impacts and extreme accidents to focus on mechanical interaction with seawater and rain.
Discretize space into fixed cubic cells and count distances/heights in cell-side units, with a=5 mm used as an example.
Require every upper layer to be no larger than and physically supported by the layer below.
Represent tides with a sum of sinusoidal functions and use a fixed wave period T_w for repeated sea-wave impacts.
Replace successive varying local speeds with printed average-speed relations and assume constant acceleration/deceleration.
Treat viscous force as the aggregate of friction, electrostatic interaction, and liquidity effects through an empirical curve.
Idealize a grain as a sphere for Stokes resistance and aggregate many grains into one cell coefficient gamma.
Set the fluid speed beneath an upper-surface sand cell to zero in the Bernoulli reduction.
Treat raindrop impact as much stronger than gravity and cell viscosity for multi-face-exposed cells.

contributions.summary: A three-dimensional cellular automaton represents supported wet-sand cells, mixture state, gradients, and local transition rules rather than assuming one fixed analytic shape.
A tide-to-shallow-wave branch creates time-varying exposure and unequal front/back speed inputs for cellular erosion.
A mixture-dependent viscous-force fit is shared by slide, scouring, and floatage branches, exposing the intended material-mechanism coupling.
A sandpile-inspired local-gradient rule turns cellular self-stability into deterministic or probabilistic slides and possible cascades.
Eight scouring topologies and five floatage topologies convert neighbor geometry into explicit cell-removal inequalities.
Rain receives a distinct exposed-face transition and a separate proportional water-uptake update rather than being treated as another seawater wave.
Residual ratio supplies a common-time response that avoids declaring an arbitrary failure threshold.
Stable-platform cross sections are fed back as new embryos, producing an interpretable shell-shaped A-B-C design through iteration.
Separate dry and rainy mixture traversals report k=0.38/K=2.63 and k=0.37/K=2.70 with ratio direction explicit.
A ten-level rainfall sweep and a stakeholder article carry model outputs into sensitivity boundaries and practical construction advice.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Tables 1-2 provide the source nomenclature, but K/k reciprocity and several later symbol overloads require a denominator-and-section ledger.
Figure 2 supplies four approximately equal-volume initial states at s=0.5, 1, 1.5, and 2; exact occupied-cell arrays are not published.
Figure 3 supplies the plotted tide boundary and 06:00-22:00 access context without machine-readable observations or sinusoidal coefficients.
Figure 5 and cited granular-matter discussion motivate k_bar=0.445, but Equation (11)'s coefficients and fitting data are absent.

Table 3 supplies eight exact scouring inequalities: Case 1 F_i>3f+N; Case 2 (sqrt(2)/2)F_i>3f; Case 3 F_i>f+N; Case 4 F_i>2f; Case 5 F_i>5f+N; Case 6 (sqrt(2)/2)F_i>4f; Case 7 F_i>3f+N; Case 8 F_i>3f.
Table 4 supplies five exact floatage inequalities: F_lift>2f+G, 3f+G, 3f+G, 4f+G, and 5f+G for Cases 1-5.
Equation (26) defines lambda relative to average rainfall and beta as absorption, but neither benchmark rainfall nor beta is quantified.
Dry shape runs fix initial k=0.445, submerge height 6 cm, approximately equal cell counts, and three reported gradients for a 120-minute comparison.
The dry ratio plot covers three elapsed times and reports k=0.38; the rainy branch visibly prints initial k=0.045 and lambda=1 before its 30-minute gradient comparison.
The rainfall sensitivity plot uses ten lambda values 0.3, 0.6, ..., 3.0 relative to Florida annual-average precipitation, but gives no raw rainfall time series or conversion.

models.summary: Represent a feasible sandcastle foundation as supported cubic cells and generate initial layers from an embryo and gradient.
Represent twice-daily tide variation and recreational opening hours as a changing submergence boundary.
Convert local water depth into the wave-speed scale used by the erosion branch.
Compute unequal local speeds at the front and back of a sloping foundation.
Collapse the two unequal local speed histories into the paper's overall average impact-speed proxy.
Represent the friction-electrostatic-liquidity tradeoff and locate the mixture that maximizes cell-to-cell resistance.
Use local column-height differences and normalized viscosity to decide whether a surface cell slides and may trigger collapse.
Aggregate grain-level Stokes resistance into cell impact force and compare it with viscous/support resistance for eight neighbor configurations.
Convert pressure difference across a surface cell into lift and compare it with viscosity and gravity for five exposed-neighbor configurations.
Separate raindrop-driven water uptake from immediate cell removal based on exposed faces.
Update a hit cell's water-to-sand ratio after each seawater wave contact.
Update Category I cells under rain using absorption capacity and relative rainfall.
Compare foundations by the fraction of initial cells remaining after the same erosion time.

models.family: cellular simulation with fixed-point-inspired shape search
models.summary: Compare gradients and iteratively reuse a stable cross section to obtain the dry shell-shaped A-B-C foundation.
Select the dry water-to-sand ratio using residual-ratio curves at several elapsed times.
Select a steeper rain-conditioned A-B-C shape and then choose its mixture ratio.
Translate mechanisms into construction advice and test residual trajectories across relative rainfall 0.3-3.0.
Summarize the bounded model outputs and translate them into a public construction recipe without promoting unsupported claims.

results_trace.summary: For dry erosion, s=0.5 initially loses cells faster but later exceeds steeper candidates; the source therefore favors a milder initial gradient for the chosen tide-wave setting.
Stepwise residual curves are interpreted as a ladder effect: platform intervals correspond to temporarily stable cellular shapes before water uptake weakens viscosity and triggers further loss.

Repeated embryo updates converge visually to a shell-shaped foundation with Part A buffering/decelerating water, Part B cutting off and further mitigating flow, and Part C storing most sand in a stable back bulk.
The dry mixture sweep reports water-to-sand k=0.38 and reciprocal sand-to-water K=2.63, expressed as 2.63 liters sand per liter seawater.
The rainy setup visibly prints initial k=0.045, lambda=1, and selects gradient s=1.5 at 30 minutes; 0.045 remains an unresolved conflict with 0.445.
The rain-conditioned ideal shape is steeper, retains A-B-C functions, and reports R=0.91 after 30 minutes versus below 0.8 for basic-embryo shapes of the same volume.
The rainy mixture sweep reports k=0.37 and reciprocal K=2.70.
At 15 minutes under lambda=3.0, residual ratio is below 0.4; under lambda=0.3 it remains above 0.9, supporting sensitivity only within the internal model.

Practical strategies are to build after the stated peak period, cover or support the foundation, maintain moisture, consider binder/cement where allowed, and use finer/purer sand, all conditional on unmodeled safety and environmental effects.
The public article translates the dry recipe to 1 liter sand plus 0.38 liter water and uses the A-B-C geometry narrative, but its wind/sunshine-analysis claim has no body evidence.

weaknesses.summary: Equations (8)-(10) define v_bar, v_bar_1, and v_bar_2 mutually and implicitly, but the paper supplies no solve order, initialization, iteration rule, branch selection, convergence criterion, or proof that the chosen average represents wave impact.

Equation (11) visibly contains two exponential branches but prints no branch conditions; a consumer must retain both expressions and must not invent whether k is above or below k_bar until source code, derivation, or an authoritative correction is available.

Equation (14) visibly prints its final normalized-viscosity interval as 0.8 <= f_N >= 1; the malformed inequality is retained verbatim and cannot be silently replaced with the likely intended interval.

Equation (16) compresses the grain-level Stokes resistance into F_i=gamma mu, but gamma has no calibrated value, unit, derivation, grain-count relation, diameter distribution, exposed-area term, or uncertainty account.
Equation (18) prints rho Delta h_0 after Equation (17) used rho g h; the missing g creates a dimensional inconsistency that is not silently repaired even though Equation (24) later restores rho g V.

Section 5.4 visibly sets the rainy initial water-to-sand proportion to 0.045, conflicting with the 0.445 peak and initial value stated elsewhere; both values remain in the record until code or source data establishes which was used.

The magazine article claims that wind, sunshine, and other environmental factors were analyzed, but no corresponding model, parameter, result, figure, table, or body discussion appears in the paper; the claim is unsupported rather than merely omitted for brevity.
